category: multi-hoster / debrid with cloud storage and seedbox

free_tier.stated: A free tier exists but its allowance is not published in the API documentation. The API types accounts explicitly - 'accountType: 0 = Free, 1 = Premium, 2 = Lifetime premium' and 'premiumLeft: Number of seconds remaining for premium status, always 0 for free users' - and the site describes itself as 'Premium link generator and Seedbox, partially free'. The daily quota exists as error codes maxLink ('Daily link limit reached') and maxData ('Daily data limit reached'), with no number attached anywhere in the reference.
free_tier.notes: unit 'none' means no allowance is stated, not that the tier is empty: free accounts get keys and a daily budget whose size the vendor does not write down.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable to unrestrict. Torrent size is capped with 'torrentTooBig - The torrent is too big or have too many files', with no number published.

retention.stated: Cloud files live under /files/{idParent}/list until deleted; torrents live in the seedbox list. No expiry is published for either.

egress.terms: No byte allowance published. Two account-level daily meters are enforced instead: maxData and maxDataHost ('Daily data limit reached' and 'for this host'), plus maxLink and maxLinkHost for link counts.

interface_detail: REST v2 at https://debrid-link.com/api/v2/ (host also answers as debrid-link.fr), authenticated with a private API key from /webapp/apikey or with an OAuth2 access_token; v1 additionally supported a timestamped X-DL-TOKEN/X-DL-SIGN/X-DL-TS signature scheme. OAuth2 device-code and auth-code flows are documented at /api_doc/v2/oauth2-device-code and /oauth2-auth-code. No WebDAV or filesystem interface was found in the method list.
tooling: rdt-client and Decypharr both support it for *arr; Torrentio supports it for Stremio; there is a community MCP server and zurg nightlies add a backend. No rclone backend of its own.
chaining: The one API here whose documentation is itself a machine-readable JSON endpoint (/api/v2/api_doc/infos plus /api_doc/errors), which means a client can generate its own bindings and refresh them without scraping; pair it with Decypharr for *arr.

limits_note: The throttle is one hour, not one minute, and it is per endpoint rather than per account. A retry loop that re-hammers the same endpoint converts a short burst into an hour of downtime, which is the failure mode a naive exponential backoff still walks into.
binding_note: The daily data meter on the account is what ends a 1 TiB/month workload on a free key; the request rate only bites when a client polls a single endpoint, and its penalty is an hour rather than a minute.

identity_cost.detail: Email only for a free account, which is issued an API key; premium needs a payment method. The API key page is https://debrid-link.com/webapp/apikey.

reliability_note: The documentation site is a JavaScript application: both docs.debrid-link.com and the rendered /api_doc/v2/* pages return an empty shell to a plain reader, and /api_doc/v2/introduction returns 200 with the body replaced by 'Loading ...'. Only the JSON endpoints behind it carry the text.
confidence_note: The vendor's own machine-readable documentation endpoints were read today, including the method list with per-method login flags and the full error table. The free tier's size is the one gap: the vendor publishes the error code but not the number, so no quota figure appears in this record.

notes: The self-description 'partially free' plus the existence of maxLink/maxData is as far as the evidence goes on the free tier; do not confuse that with a published quota. Abandonment condition: if /api/v2/api_doc/infos ever carries a limits block, replace the 'unpublished' fields with numbers. The vendor's own two pages give 41 and 42 hosts the record keeps 41, which is the number on the page a buyer reads. There is no annual plan: the ladder stops at 300 days for 25 EUR. The free tier is real but undocumented in public, which is itself the finding: a reader cannot know what it buys without creating an account. The premium page says 41 hosts and the live API lists 43, so the marketing count lags the API. No host in the live list carries isFree:true, while the vendor's own documentation sample does - the free-host set appears to have been emptied. A textbook case of a stable price hiding a shrinking product: the euro figure is byte-identical across 37 months while the host count falls 173 -> 164 -> 53 -> 41, a 76% loss. Any table that compares this service by price alone ranks it first and is wrong. Classified as undetermined in the matrix because the vendor checkout could not be read. The reseller route is real and vendor-published, which is enough to say a cardless client can buy it, but not enough to say the vendor takes crypto. Candidates for the first failure: the flood refusal, the 20-slot ceiling, or a per-host daily quota. The flood refusal is the only one with a stated duration and the only one the client treats as an hour-long park. The vendor's own error table could not be read, which is the main gap in this record. Technically the best-shaped small debrid for automation, and the one whose retention is least documented. Abandonment condition: if no retention statement appears by the next pass, keep the null and stop asking; a WebDAV listing after a lapse is the only route that answers it.

extras.auth_flows: two: a private API key from the webapp (single header), or OAuth2 with a device-code flow (/oauth2-device-code), an auth-code flow (/oauth2-auth-code) and a refresh endpoint. Refresh tokens issue one access_token per authorization and the old one is revoked on refresh.
extras.unrestrict_endpoint: POST /downloader/add; metadata and readiness through GET /downloader/list and GET /downloader/limits
extras.account_endpoints: GET /account/infos (username, email, emailVerified, accountType, premiumLeft, pts, upgradeAccountUrl)
extras.public_endpoints_no_account: GET /downloader/hosts, GET /downloader/domains, GET /downloader/regex, GET /stream/transcode/:id/infos - the login:false methods in the method list
extras.doc_discovery: the rendered docs are an Angular app; the content is reachable only through /api/v2/api_doc/infos and /api/v2/api_doc/errors, which is worth knowing before the next session files this as 'docs behind a login'
extras.annual_plan: none; 300 days is the longest term

extras.account_states: badToken / badSign (credential); floodDetected (hour park); maxTorrent, maxData, maxLink and Host variants (quota); serverNotAllowed, maintenanceHost, maxTransfer (temporarily unavailable); badId (torrent gone)
extras.cache_miss: no cache-check endpoint exists; the add response is the only signal, and an uncached add downloads like any other
extras.host_removal: maintenanceHost and serverNotAllowed are per-request signals; no public announcement page was found
extras.simultaneous_use: No IP or device rule on the pages read. The documented concurrency limits are 20 active slots and 8 API requests.
